one_star_reviews.text:
A very disappointing experience with Iberia. We've been trying to resolve an access problem to my husband's account for over four weeks. First, we had to wait weeks to update the email address, and even after updating it, we still couldn't change the password.

During all this time, we contacted customer service several times, and the response was always the same: wait 72 hours. Weeks have passed, and we still have no solution.

Today, after being told they would try to contact us within the hour with an update, we waited again without receiving any response. Finally, they informed us that the email address change hadn't been synced correctly and that the case had been sent to another department, without being able to give us a specific timeframe for resolution.

The most frustrating thing is that we need to buy our Christmas tickets, and we can't properly use our account or the terms and conditions associated with the Iberia card we signed up for. We specifically applied for the card because our intention was to start using Iberia as our regular airline, accumulate points, and consolidate our travel with them.

After this experience, we have lost confidence in Iberia and have decided to buy our next tickets with another airline. We will also be filing a formal complaint with Iberia and taking the matter to the consumer protection agency.

For a problem that should be easily resolved, more than four weeks of waiting, multiple contacts, and repeated 72-hour delays without a solution make this a very disappointing customer service experience.

one_star_reviews.text:
I tried getting my second prosthesis made at this center, and honestly, it almost gave me a breakdown. The prosthesis was huge and incredibly heavy, deforming my eye. The brown was nothing like my natural eye color, and the white was a stark white, completely unlike my other eye. It was awful. To make matters worse, during one of the appointments, he dared to ask me what was worse: losing an eye to disease rather than the way I had lost mine. He certainly wasn't in a position to judge because he hadn't experienced either situation.

And another time, when I went to bring him the prosthesis because it was hideous—everyone was telling me so—he tried to file it down to make it fit better. He also made a mistake by not writing down the 150 euros he charged me, because he also charged me 250 euros for the 3D impression. My first prosthetist didn't charge me a single euro for that, and his work was hand-painted and turned out twenty times better than his method. He humiliated me terribly in front of everyone waiting, telling me to look in my bank account for the €150 receipt. This was after he'd already charged me for the prescription and then charged me an additional €250 for a small bottle of cleaning solution that cost €10.

He practically forced me to take it and pay for it. The first prosthetist I mentioned, who is the best in all of Seville, gave me suction cups and cleaning solution for the prosthesis. I just want to make it clear that this man is still wondering why most people go to the best prosthetist in Seville. The answer is: because he creates works of art, not shoddy work.

Today, Tuesday, August 18th, I was shopping at this Álvaro Moreno store, and the experience exceeded all limits of professionalism and rudeness. I felt like a criminal; never in my life have I been treated so badly, nor have you ever made me feel so bad in a store.

From the very first moment, the two employees displayed absolute distrust, treating us like thieves and constantly questioning the clothes we had in the fitting room. The situation reached an unacceptable point when one of the employees even entered the fitting room while my partner was in his underwear, all because of her obsessive distrust of the clothes I had previously shown her we had.
The worst part is not only the degrading treatment and invasion of privacy, but also the response when we filed a complaint: far from apologizing for such an unpleasant situation, they hid behind the excuse that "there are only two people working," as if that justified disrespecting customers and violating their privacy.

Terrible service, intolerable lack of respect, and a complete absence of professionalism. I will never set foot in this store again.

Terrible service and a suspicious arrangement with a local garage.

I was extremely disappointed with the service I received from the tow truck driver (a man in his fifties with light eyes).

His job should have been to help us solve the problem as quickly and efficiently as possible, but instead, he was only interested in selling us the option that suited him best.

We had a simple flat tire and the spare was ready; any professional with even a little bit of effort would have changed the tire in five minutes so we could continue on our way.

Instead, he made a thousand excuses not to change it and blatantly insisted on taking us to a specific garage. The result: a shocking €70 rip-off for fixing a flat tire.

It all reeks of an agreement or kickback between the tow truck driver and the garage, taking advantage of the customer's desperation.

A complete lack of professional ethics and outright abuse. I absolutely do not recommend this service if you don't want to be taken advantage of.

one_star_reviews.text:
⭐ 1/5

An absolutely unacceptable experience.

I gave a package to an employee at this store to handle its shipment. The employee claimed the package had been sent and later showed me a photo as supposed proof, but never provided me with a tracking number or any valid receipt.

After trying to locate the package, I discovered there was no record of it being shipped. The company itself confirmed that the package doesn't appear in their system and that they can't locate it. To this day, no one knows where my package is or what happened to it.

The worst part is that the employee who received and handled the package stopped responding to my messages and hasn't been able to explain what she did with it.

I'm not talking about a minor mistake or a delay. When someone receives a customer's package and is responsible for shipping it, there should be a minimum level of responsibility, professionalism, and traceability. If something goes wrong, the least they can do is inform the customer and find a solution.

My experience with this employee was one of utter unprofessionalism. I believe that someone who handles shipments this way shouldn't be serving customers or handling other people's packages.

I strongly advise anyone using this store to be extremely careful and not to hand over any package without immediately obtaining an official receipt and tracking number.

one_star_reviews.text:
I bought a watch on August 4th and it stopped working on August 9th. I think they probably sold it to me defective, because it's not normal for that to happen so quickly.
I took it back to the store and the saleswoman told me they would have to send it to Seville to be checked.
To this day, I'm still waiting for a response, and it looks like it will take forever. She warned me that it usually takes more than 20 days for the watch to be back in the store, but since they're on vacation, I might be waiting forever... Based on my experience, I will never buy from that store again, or any other "Time Road" store.
The company's policy, in my opinion, leaves much to be desired, to be honest.
If someone had explained to me that it would take so long to resolve a problem (which might even just be a battery replacement, who knows?)... I would have decided against buying the watch there. I absolutely do not recommend buying any of their products. I'm quite disappointed with the treatment I'm receiving.

one_star_reviews.text:
Before beginning this review, I'd like to emphasize that my intention is not to disrespect anyone. I simply want to share my experience so that others can consider different options before consulting Francisco Montesinos.
I will now list the reasons why he didn't benefit me, including the exorbitant price per session: In the eight sessions I had with Francisco, I don't recall addressing the issues that were causing my life to be so disorganized. The sessions were based on meditation, which, in 80% of cases, led me to fall asleep. We didn't analyze why I was doing what I was doing; the only solution he offered when those thoughts arose was to meditate.
I felt betrayed and abandoned because, in the first session, he implied that those eight sessions were highly effective. Therefore, even though I wasn't satisfied, I continued after the second session, despite the financial strain it was causing me.

one_star_reviews.text:
I had a very disappointing experience, mainly because I felt that important information about the apartment was deliberately hidden from me. The Spotahome listing stated that the apartment had two bedrooms and that I would be living with the landlord. In reality, there was an additional bedroom occupied by another man. I later discovered that the landlord was leaving Barcelona and that another man would be moving in as well. This meant that I unexpectedly had to live with two men, which I would never have agreed to had I known this from the beginning.
I also felt that the landlord and Spotahome were not transparent about the actual layout and living arrangements. The listing should have clearly stated that there were three bedrooms and disclosed that the landlord would be leaving and another tenant would be moving in. I felt misled and, frankly, that the information was being hidden from me in order to rent the room.

Regarding the empadronamiento, the landlord initially refused to register me. She later agreed, but when I moved out, she refused to return my deposit unless I first removed my name from the padrón.

The contract also stated that the common areas would be cleaned every two weeks, which did not happen as agreed. Finally, €20 was deducted from my deposit for cleaning, although I left the room and bathroom clean and the contract did not specify this deduction.

Overall, the lack of transparency about the apartment, the other tenants, the registration, and the deposit made this a very uncomfortable and disappointing experience. Had I been given the full and accurate information before booking, I would not have rented the room.

one_star_reviews.text: On August 29th, around 4:30 PM, I went to this store hoping to buy several units of an item, which would have been a good sale for the business. I was helped by Carmen and a colleague who seemed to be the manager, a woman with white hair. I asked them if they could tell me if any of their stores had the item, or if I could pick it up when it arrived, or if there was any other way to get it. To every suggestion, the answer was "NO." When I finally got them to call and ask if any stores had it, and after returning 20 minutes later to give them time to answer, the manager was in the stockroom. I asked Carmen if she knew anything and told her I was waiting. After another 20 minutes of waiting for the manager to come out, I asked Carmen again if she could please let her know I was there; I just needed to know if it was available or not. She told me she couldn't let her know, that it was impossible. After 40 minutes, I had to leave without being able to find the person in charge and without knowing if I would be able to find the item. Although neither of them made much of an effort to facilitate a good sale despite offering several alternatives, Carmen's service, in particular, left much to be desired, since after seeing me waiting there the whole time, she didn't bother to go and tell her colleague. It's a shame that employees like that give the store such a bad image.

one_star_reviews.text:
I wholeheartedly agree with all the previous negative comments. My experience fully aligns with many of the criticisms made: a lack of empathy, insufficient staff, and the attention I've received from some of the staff is appalling and, at times, arrogant.
The facilities convey a worrying sense of neglect and lack of maintenance. And, regarding those responsible for directing and managing the residence, my perception couldn't be more negative. I particularly miss a greater commitment, a willingness to listen, and a genuine commitment to resolving the problems raised by families.
The secretary's attitude struck me as arrogant and unresponsive, while the president seems to lack much more involvement in addressing the situations that arise. Ultimately, when a family entrusts a residence with the care of an elderly person, they expect something as basic as empathy, respect, attention, and solutions, not constant excuses.
It's also difficult not to question the level of trust within the residence itself when the president doesn't have his own mother there and has opted for a different, religiously affiliated residence. Each family is free to make their own decisions, of course, but I understand that this can raise questions and make one wonder why.

Ultimately, I believe there is much room for improvement: more staff, more empathy, better care, decent facilities, and above all, a management team that listens to families and is truly committed. Our elderly deserve much more than evasive answers and excuses.

one_star_reviews.text:
The place is open to both guests staying at the resort and people passing by, which sounds like a nice option. However, our experience as visitors was quite frustrating.

We were a large family, so naturally the order took a little longer. It took around 17 minutes for our order to be ready, but the resort staff came to remind us that the parking spots are limited to 15 minutes and insisted that we leave.

The problem is that, after being told to move the car, getting back to the area is not that simple. The roads around here are quite long and curvy, and making a quick loop is not really practical, especially with a large family and kids.

If the café is going to promote itself as being open to people passing by, there should be a more practical solution for parking. Otherwise, I think it would be better to stop promoting it to passersby, because the current setup can create a pretty frustrating experience.

Parking on the street also doesn’t feel like the safest option when you’re traveling with kids.

And after all that, I almost forgot to mention that the place itself is actually quite nice. Unfortunately, I wasn’t as impressed with the coffee. For a place presenting itself as a specialty coffee shop, I expected a higher level of coffee quality.

one_star_reviews.text: This review is by the manager of the betting shop. I went there a few years ago during the summer when I usually spend my holidays in Huelva, and I desperately needed a bathroom after arriving from the ferry from Portugal. So, if the manager has changed since then, he should know it's not for him. I went into this betting shop because I always use betting shops to go to the bathroom, since I suppose that because they use sick people to withdraw money, they don't usually dare to tell me to go to the bathroom without spending anything. Besides, I'm very clean and don't make a mess. Well, when I was about to leave, the manager came up to me and got cocky, telling me that it was a gambling establishment and that you go there to bet, not to use the bathroom. I didn't dwell on him and just said "okay, okay," hurrying to get out of there quickly. You have to have some serious nerve to dare complain about someone using your bathroom (without making a mess, by the way) when you're making a living in the most exploitative way possible. It's no wonder you're so irritable, having to run a business like that in a town like Ayamonte, which is practically deserted in winter. If God or divine justice exists, I'm absolutely certain they'll make you pay for all the harm your business brings to the world.

one_star_reviews.text: Very unprofessional and lacking in empathy
Take care of yourselves and your families, and compare and seek opinions from other professionals and clinics before hiring anything here. That's my humble advice.

I remember this man with a bad feeling. Many years ago, I had a substance abuse problem. I weighed 60 kg and knew I didn't want to continue, but I was experiencing brutal withdrawal symptoms. I went to the hospital, and this "gentleman" saw me after triage in a glass-enclosed room. I told him what was happening, and he said he wasn't going to admit me or give me anything, that this wasn't a clinic, and that if I had withdrawal symptoms, I was old enough to know what I was doing—basically, that I should just deal with it. To add insult to injury, he only gave me a printed copy of the medication I was already taking. It seemed like a very strange report considering how little time he spent typing. Later, I discovered what he had entered about me on the My Health portal, which he hadn't printed out and given me. Do you remember me now?

Now I weigh 110 kg of pure muscle. I'm cured, and I work as an advisor to other personal trainers.

I don't know if he would accept, but if he holds consultations here, I would like him to listen to me so he can learn how to treat a patient who comes to the Emergency Room because he wants to get out of the dark place.
absolute lack of tact and a minimum of humanity and understanding towards the patient

one_star_reviews.text:
As a property manager, I absolutely do not recommend their services. They have only brought problems to our community.

We worked with them for a year until we finally had to terminate our contract. I could list a long series of issues that were systematically ignored, and the few that were addressed were left unfinished due to misunderstandings.

At the last meeting, we asked for transparency, and their response was that they were overwhelmed with work. We understand that the overload is not the fault of the staff, but the reality is that they haven't resolved anything in a year.

They are even creating obstacles to the transfer to the new management company, making it difficult to provide us with the necessary documentation.

Deplorable management.

Not recommended at all; I'd only recommend them to my worst enemy.

I live in the Ámbar building, owned by CSB. They work with Civitas, and we made the huge mistake of staying with them instead of changing management companies. In the new building—the Jade—they were smarter: they got rid of them at the first meeting.

In a whole year, they haven't done a single thing. CSB didn't install a mirror for us to safely enter and exit the garage; we complained through them, and they gave us a flimsy one (anyone who wants to can go and see for themselves).

When you entered the garage, the lights didn't turn on; we did the same thing, and they installed a motion sensor at the entrance that only activates when you drive in, leaving the other part of the garage in the dark. We informed Civitas about this, and they replied by asking if we wanted the whole garage to light up (which is laughable), and it's still like that....

The fire door springs in the building made a terrible banging noise; We notified them, and they adjusted some of the shutters, but they said others had to be replaced and gave us a quote of X euros. We told them that, since the building is new and less than a year old, the shutters should be under warranty, and they replied that they had to check (in Spain and Europe, the legal warranty is three years, something I think everyone knows), and that's how it remains...

Then, a large majority of the residents want to install glass curtains. Every time you ask them something, they give you the runaround and say they don't know. I imagine that, out of the 150 communities they manage—just to give an example—some must have done it, and it can't be that complicated when all new buildings have them. But, hey, we must be the only community in Gijón where they can't be installed.

In short: a completely wasted year with them. If you hear "Civitas," run...

one_star_reviews.text:
I personally attended a baptism at this Church. I was there, I saw it with my own eyes, and I left with even more questions than when I arrived.

And that's why I want to say something I feel is necessary: ​​before you get baptized here, know the full history of the institution you're entering.

Because yes: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints has a history of racial discrimination against Black people that shouldn't be glossed over.

For more than a century, Black men were excluded from the priesthood, and Black people were excluded from certain temple ordinances. And this wasn't simply an administrative rule. For decades, religious explanations were given to justify this inequality.

There was talk of the curse of Cain and the mark of Cain, associating them with the Black population. There were also teachings that linked race to the so-called curse of Ham and to people's supposed faithfulness during a premortal existence.

In other words, for generations, people were told, within a religious context, that their race was linked to a curse and that, therefore, they could not enjoy the same religious opportunities.
That happened.

And the fact that those restrictions were lifted in 1978 doesn't erase that history.

Today, the Church itself rejects those old explanations. Fine. But then why not talk about them openly when someone is considering baptism?

Why should someone have to discover later that the institution they have just placed their trust in held those teachings about Black people for generations?

I, too, saw religious practices there that were completely foreign to me. I saw the laying on of hands forming a circle around the person being baptized and other ceremonies that, from my own faith, I don't identify with how I understand the search for Jesus Christ.

And here I'm going to be very clear: for me, those doctrines and those rituals do not represent the God in whom I believe. From my Christian perspective, I consider these teachings false, and I believe this Church deviates profoundly from the Christianity I know.

There is also a very specific economic teaching: tithing 10% of income.

And then there is the Book of Mormon. Joseph Smith claimed to have received gold plates and translated them through revelation. The Church considers it sacred scripture; for me, that claim does not constitute divine revelation, and I do not accept that doctrine.
I also do not accept their conception of God or the teaching that human beings can become like God.

For all these reasons, I consider this a sect and a false doctrine. That is my personal and religious assessment, and I have the right to express it.

But there is something that worries me even more. I saw people from different backgrounds entering there, feeling welcomed, finding a community, and trusting what they were told. And precisely for that reason, I believe they also have the right to know the uncomfortable side of the story.

It is not enough that they smile at you today.

It's not enough to be told you've found a family here.

It's not enough for someone to make you feel special.
Investigate before surrendering your faith.
Investigate the racial history of this Church.

Investigate the curse of Cain.

Investigate what was taught about Black people.

Investigate what changed in 1978 and why.

Investigate its scriptures.

Investigate its doctrines about God.

Investigate its ceremonies.

Investigate tithing.

And then decide.

Because I was there. And precisely because I was there, I don't intend to remain silent, pretending I didn't see or feel anything.

I'm not saying that everyone who comes here is racist. I'm saying something much more concrete and much harder to deny:

an institution can change its current rhetoric, but it cannot erase its history.

And a person who is going to surrender their faith to an institution deserves to know the whole story: the beautiful and the shameful.

one_star_reviews.text: I regret to say that my experience with AEDAS Homes on the Carena Waves development in El Médano has been very disappointing, especially considering it's a national developer from whom one would expect seriousness and respect for commitments made. I signed a preliminary sales agreement in January 2025 and, for nearly two years, agreed to sign five consecutive extensions, most of them for periods of only two or three months. With each new extension, AEDAS fueled my hopes by stating that, pending only minor details, the granting of the building permit and the start of construction were imminent. They kept me waiting all that time, convinced that I had a contractually reserved home and without exploring other options. Now, AEDAS is informing me that, citing the time that has passed, they intend to unilaterally and prematurely terminate the preliminary sales agreement, which would mean two lost years for me and cause serious harm on all levels.

one_star_reviews.text:
My experience today, August 18th, around 8:40 PM, at Kiabi in the Arena Shopping Center was quite unpleasant.

There were three people in line, and since I was going to pay by card, I headed to the self-checkout to speed things up. As I approached the terminal, a young woman with glasses came out of her station and came directly to help me, practically without giving me time to even put the clothes away or start the process.

She told me I had to pay for the bag even before I had started paying, asked me about the hangers, and began handling the clothes and the bag quite hurriedly, barely giving me a chance to react. The situation made me feel very uncomfortable because I didn't understand the reason for so much supervision.

If a customer goes to the self-checkout, especially when there are other people waiting in line, the normal thing to do would be to let them shop normally and help them if they need assistance.

In my case, I was obviously going to pay for everything. I have no interest in taking 20-cent hangers or refusing to pay for a three-euro t-shirt. I simply don't need the hangers and would prefer to pay and leave, like any other customer.

I completely understand that staff need to monitor self-checkout and prevent errors or losses, but how they do it is important. I found the service excessively intrusive and, above all, it made me feel like I was being distrusted for no reason whatsoever.

I hope you can review these situations, because monitoring self-checkout shouldn't mean making customers feel suspicious while they're simply trying to pay for their purchases.

one_star_reviews.text:
The worst real estate agency I've ever encountered. Run from them. I've dealt with real estate agencies throughout my life, but never with one like this. They've been reported to the authorities. Keep reading to the end so you don't go through what we did.

They're a family business run by Miguel, his wife Carolina, and their son Alexis. We rented an apartment through them, and instead of collecting the commission from the property owner as is legally required, they charged us (they have a lawsuit to recover my money). From the very beginning, Miguel's treatment of everyone left much to be desired, and even at the contract signing, they overlooked the additional guarantee (the second month's deposit); in other words, there was no signed document. I paid two months' deposit, the current month's rent, and the agency commission (one month's rent), but only one month's deposit was listed. So, according to the contract, we had only paid the current month's rent and one month's deposit. They think we fell from a tree. With these people, it's one constant lack of transparency after another. However, they insist on cash payments, and they're very insistent...

When we first walked into the apartment, it was like a house of horrors: the microwave was burnt out, the refrigerator was overflowing with ice, the washing machine's rubber seal was rotten, the curtains were torn, and the floor was filthy—your hands would stick to the kitchen counter. They tried to take advantage of us because we were desperate to rent, and with the excuse that they were quick to let us in, they didn't do anything, not even halfway through. Miguel told us, "That's just how it is..." and if we didn't fix it, they'd tell us to leave. This was on the very day we signed the contract, and they wouldn't even give us a copy. They wanted us to leave with the keys, having left more than three thousand euros on the table, but without the contract. Three copies of the contract were signed, and they only gave me a photocopy, claiming they had to take it to the Chamber of Commerce to register it. They said they'd fix everything, only to later say they wouldn't fix anything. They wanted us to pay for the repairs ourselves, which I refused from the start. They're very friendly with tenants on the first day when they collect their commission, but from the next day on, they completely ignore you. They also demanded payment on the 1st of every month, even though the legal payment dates in the contract are between the 1st and 5th.

Finally, after a year, we received a letter from the landlord stating that we had to vacate the apartment. This Miguel guy came to the apartment, banging on my door in front of all the neighbors and yelling at me to leave, subjecting me to intolerable public humiliation and implying to the neighbors that I wasn't paying, even though I've been a scrupulously punctual tenant every month. In fact, he chased me out into the street, displaying extremely violent and aggressive behavior, repeatedly hurling insults. Completely intolerable and dangerous behavior.

This real estate agency is currently facing a lawsuit from me for charging an illegal commission that, according to current Housing Law, should have been charged to the property owner, not me. This was their and the owner's objective: to keep us in the apartment for a year, charge us an illegal commission, and then evict us with the "recovery of the property due to necessity" clause (we lost all our appliances). Run from these people because their business practices are disastrous for any tenant's interests. They will deny everything I've said here; don't say I didn't warn you.

one_star_reviews.text:
This has undoubtedly been one of the most painful and disappointing experiences we have ever had.

We went to this clinic full of hope to start a family and trusted their professional judgment completely. After a single ovarian stimulation, in our case, no prior blood test was performed to assess estradiol levels before starting the stimulation. Four follicles were retrieved, but only one developed, and it was too large. We were told that the chances of that single follicle developing were practically nonexistent and were advised not to continue.
We ourselves suggested the possibility of undergoing another stimulation, and as many as necessary, with the intention of trying to accumulate more follicles. It was then that we received a response we will never forget: they told us that we would probably never be able to obtain more follicles, or even fewer, and that our only option was egg donation.
We made it clear that egg donation was not an option for us. And that's when, essentially, they made us understand that if we didn't accept egg donation, we should forget about having a child.

Imagine what it's like to hear something like that when you're placing your hopes, your trust, and also your money in a fertility clinic.
Fortunately, we decided to get a second opinion. We went to another clinic, explained exactly what had happened, and the gynecologist who saw us was surprised by our case. She explained that there were options, that before giving up on our case, certain parameters needed to be studied, and that the treatment could be adjusted depending on our response.
The corresponding tests were performed, estradiol levels were assessed—something that wasn't done at this clinic—and the medication was adjusted. And here's the part we still find hard to believe: We only needed ovarian stimulation to achieve our goal.
Today we have a three-month-old baby.

That's why, beyond the money we spent at this clinic, what truly hurts is thinking that we almost accepted our dream of becoming parents was over because a medical team told us there were no alternatives for us.

We don't question that every woman responds differently to treatments, nor that assisted reproduction can be a complicated path. We also don't expect anyone to guarantee a pregnancy. What we do expect from a specialized clinic is that they study our case individually, evaluate the existing alternatives, and don't make us feel that our desire to be parents ends after a single attempt.

We decided not to accept that answer and sought a second opinion. And thanks to that decision, and to the professionalism of the gynecologist who treated us afterward, we now have our son in our arms.

It's impossible not to wonder what would have happened if we had accepted that first assessment as final.
To anyone going through a similar situation, we would say seek a second opinion before giving up. We did, and it changed our lives. This review is not intended to question the existence of difficult cases or the possibility that a treatment might not work. It is simply our experience, and our experience with this clinic was profoundly negative. We would not recommend it to anyone. We left there thinking we would never be able to have children, and today we have a three-month-old baby.
That difference says it all.

one_star_reviews.text:
Alena's Review
A horrible place, poorly run, a money-grab.
If you care about your family, never leave them in these residences.
All the (extreme) prohibitions they make you sign upon entering, privately, are systematically violated inside the residence.
No drugs, yet they are consumed within the facilities. No sex, yet it happens. No food in the rooms, yet it's kept there. It's a kind of boarding school run by psychologists, a social worker, and social educators. Without meaning to disparage their professions, with two or three rare exceptions, they are very, very bad. They don't help; they systematically mistreat the residents. There's one in particular who should have retired a long time ago; she's not fit to work in a place like this.
The social worker takes forever to process paperwork, e.g., for dependency care.

The psychologist is as green as a cucumber. They think they're above the law, starting with the director of the residence, who lies more than she speaks.

It's a huge business where they squeeze every last penny out of every last penny, even for activities held outside the facility. They charge you for the van ride, even for going a mile away.
It's a disgraceful place. The residents aren't helped, they're ignored, medicated, and kept alive as long as possible. The monthly fees are exorbitant, so that as many residents as possible end up crossing the street and ending up in the nursing home.
My review is simply to raise awareness among families, so that before admitting their loved ones, they don't judge a book by its cover. It's a horrible place.
Finally, I have to mention the food. The menus are signed by a doctor, of course; there's no accounting for taste.

The food they serve both in the nursing home and the one across the street is pure garbage. If they intend for the residents to have a healthy diet, what they're serving there is pure poison, unhealthy and fatal to their health.

I don't want to elaborate further. If they truly care about their relatives, they should look for other facilities. This one is designed to make as much money as possible, at the expense of providing the poorest and cheapest service to the residents. A repulsive thirst for profit.

I had the misfortune of spending some time there, voluntarily.

On March 29th of this year at 8:42 PM, I plugged my Efun Tiger motorcycle into this charger to charge. At 9:17 PM, I removed the motorcycle and it hadn't charged, as you can see in the screenshot from the charging app. The charge dropped from 1.8 kWh to 0 kWh in an unknown amount of time, perhaps seconds or a minute. I was informed that the charger was damaged due to a short circuit and needed to be replaced, at a total cost of €1,347.87. Therefore, I opened a support ticket and sent them all the required documentation. I even filed a complaint with the consumer protection office in Vélez-Málaga, which they closed because Iberdrola responded that they were working on it. I am reopening my consumer complaint and I am not ruling out taking legal action. From April, when I filed the complaint, until now, at the end of September, the service I have received from you has been appalling. It is shameful that a company the size of Iberdrola treats its customers with such disregard.

one_star_reviews.text:
€140 FOR UNDER 15 MINUTES. A COMPLETE BAIT-AND-SWITCH EXPERIENCE.

I have been a loyal customer for years, visiting whenever I travel to this city. This experience completely destroyed my trust.

1. CLEAR AGREEMENT BEFORE PAYMENT

I explicitly told the manager which specific service I wanted. She personally introduced me to workers supposedly offering it.

I then agreed directly with the worker on an additional €100 for that service and paid €250 in total.

2. SERVICE REFUSED, UNDISCLOSED CHARGES INTRODUCED

After payment, the worker refused the agreed service. I respected her decision.

However, she then retrospectively claimed that two brief interactions she had initiated herself were chargeable extras, despite neither being agreed upon as separate paid services.

These alleged extras totalled €60, yet she insisted on charging for a full hour of extras AND the half-hour package.

The entire experience, including showering and the resulting dispute, lasted less than 15 minutes.

3. MANAGEMENT UPHELD THE CHARGES

The manager recognised discrepancies in the worker's explanation but still upheld the disputed charges. Only after I strongly challenged the situation was a partial refund reluctantly offered.

FINAL RESULT:

- Paid: €250
- Refunded: €110
- Retained: €140
- Agreed service: NEVER PROVIDED

My complaint is not about someone's right to change their mind. It is about accepting payment for an agreed service, refusing it, and retrospectively introducing charges I never authorised.

I feel deliberately misled. After years of loyalty, I have completely lost confidence in this establishment and will never return.

A terrible experience. Upon entering the room, the smell was truly unpleasant, completely unacceptable for a place like this. Furthermore, it was clear there was dust; I know this because I have allergies and react very easily, and I quickly started feeling unwell. A room should be clean and maintain a minimum level of hygiene, and this place was far from it. Offering this kind of service is unacceptable; it's disrespectful to the customer. I will not return, and I do not recommend it!

Cost me about €50 on a single withdrawal. Read this before you use it.

I asked for €500. My card is EURO-denominated. The machine still processed it as a conversion into Romanian lei — 3,047 RON, which works out at roughly 6.05 RON/EUR, far worse than the real market rate (about 5.5 RON/EUR) . My account was already in euros, so there was no conversion needed at all.

If you use this machine: when it offers you a "guaranteed rate" or asks whether to charge you in your home currency, say NO and choose to be charged in EUROS. The screen is designed so that accepting looks like the normal option.

Better still, walk to a proper bank ATM. There are several in Port d'Alcúdia and Alcúdia old town.

Six months that have been a true nightmare for our family.

My parents have been at REIF Tomares for six months, and both are completely dependent. Our experience has been very negative, especially due to the lack of attention and care we have experienced on numerous occasions.

We have had to call reception hundreds of times because they didn't come to their room to attend to them, even in situations that required urgent attention. We have also experienced medication errors and are very dissatisfied with the food.

One of the most distressing incidents was having to leave a communion and return to the residence around 9:00 or 10:00 PM because they had forgotten about our parents and hadn't put them to bed. The most outrageous thing is that I made about 20 calls, both to reception and to the residence's customer service, and they didn't answer the phone.

On another occasion, my father was in a diaper completely soaked with urine for four or five hours. We called repeatedly for them to come and attend to him, and they didn't come until several hours later.

We placed our parents in a care home so they would be cared for and looked after, not so we would have to be constantly checking on them, calling, and pleading for even basic care.

We are leaving deeply disappointed and with an overwhelming sense of helplessness. I would not recommend this care home for people with a high level of dependency.

one_star_reviews.text:
From day one, our experience with this company was utterly disappointing.

The motorhome started with a battery failure, leaving us without electricity or water. The only solution they offered was a two-and-a-half-hour drive, completely refusing to replace it at the nearest repair shop, which we ourselves located and informed the company about. They could have arranged for the battery to be replaced that same day. All this while traveling with two small children, which we consider a complete lack of consideration.

But the problems didn't end there. The refrigerator stopped working on the second day, forcing us to even throw away food. Then, during the last three days of the trip, after the battery was replaced and we had traveled, we also ran out of hot water. The most outrageous thing was the company's complete lack of response: they offered no solutions, showed no interest, and were utterly indifferent to our situation.

Furthermore, we had to cover our own camping expenses to connect the motorhome to electricity, as well as travel costs and other inconveniences directly related to the breakdowns. The company took absolutely no responsibility, yet still charged us the full rental price.

To top it all off, the rudeness and lack of respect in the way we were treated made an already difficult situation even more unpleasant.

Not to mention that they charged us for the tables and chairs even though we rented them with those included.

one_star_reviews.text: Executive Master's in Cybersecurity and Ethical Hacking. I'm not unhappy with the professors or the course content; I liked it and found it appropriate. What I didn't like was that they didn't keep their promise of internships and constantly gave me the runaround when I complained. They always tell me, "It doesn't depend on us, it depends on the companies." So why offer them if you can't guarantee them? When I ask for an estimated timeframe before they tell me anything about a job/internship, they say 8 or 9 months, which isn't realistic. I enrolled in this master's program precisely because of the advertised job placement service and the claim that a high percentage of graduates find employment. In my case, that's not true. I finished the master's program in May of this year with a GPA over 9.5 and completed my final project with a perfect score. Now that I've finished my final project, they tell me that instead of an internship, they're looking for a job for me, as if that were any easier. When I complained directly by email, they didn't even reply. It ended up being the Head of Studies who called me to give me the same excuses I mentioned earlier. It's a shame that I ended up with such a negative opinion after finishing this master's program, considering how happy and excited I was when I started. Now I've seen reviews of my same course (cybersecurity) with the same complaints I have, and if I had known this beforehand, I would have looked for another place to study.

I'm going to share my experience with these machines. I went to get my photo taken for my ID renewal. I wasn't very convinced about the photo quality because it came out tiny and too dark... In short, a bit of a disaster. Even so, I submitted it to the National Police for the document, and the officer himself was shocked by the poor quality. He told me to go to an official place, like a photo shop, and have it taken there properly.
I tried to request a refund by calling the phone number on the machine, and they gave me an email address where I had to file the complaint. They asked for some information, which I provided, all for €5, which is what the photos cost. I sent it on August 4th, and to this day, they haven't replied. I called again, and they told me that complaints are handled externally. What's going on? Isn't there anyone responsible? Please don't fall for the scams offered by these types of machines and go to a photography shop where you'll receive proper, immediate service. Thank you.

one_star_reviews.text: This happened three years ago, but I'm daring to publish it today. I asked for a quote to manage a small inheritance of €5,000, which they wanted to charge me. I still have the quote. I went to a management company and they charged me €300.

APPALLING. This company assigned us our funeral insurance, and the only thing they were good for was requesting the certificate of last will and testament.

We had a meeting where the only thing the woman I spoke with seemed to care about was repeating that "they are experts in inheritances" (thank goodness, otherwise...) and insisting on an in-person meeting to set up a provision of funds that wasn't actually necessary because all that was needed was the inheritance tax return, which is included in the insurance.

It was a very simple inheritance that could have been handled after the first call. Instead, she got bogged down in requesting documents that no one had ever asked for, creating obstacles every time I asked about the status of the process, and taking days and days to reply to any message...

Until finally, we opted to pay a professional to handle the tax, and everything was done in less than 15 days.
If it had been a more complex inheritance, I don't even want to think about what could have happened.

If you are in a position to hire another company, do it. Run away from this place because it's a complete disaster.

I worked there. Yesterday, August 28th, at 6:03/6:04 AM on Line 11, we had all just arrived for the morning shift. Not even five minutes had passed since we started our shift, so I went to my position on a stool, ready to label the products. I thought they were about to start the machine, because, as I said, not even five minutes had passed since our shift began and since we all arrived. Then a bossy woman in a blue suit came up to me and said rudely, "Don't just sit there waiting for the machine to fix itself, go help other lines." First of all, I didn't know you could go help other lines without your supervisors telling you to, and none of my supervisors told me to go help any line. I only listen to them and don't make decisions on my own. Second, at no point did I know that the machine wasn't working and that it needed fixing and would take some time. None of my supervisors informed me. As I said, I had just arrived; we hadn't even started our shift five minutes earlier, so we were still getting used to the machine and our workstations, ready to begin (or so I thought). Third, that bossy woman in blue told me in a foul tone—a haughty, aggressive, arrogant, conceited, overbearing, pedantic, and conceited tone. Instead of telling me politely, or at least in a normal way, she could have informed me that the machine wasn't working and that it would take a while to get it up and running, since I hadn't been informed, and I was doing my job: lined up at my assigned station, ready to start. Since I never once thought the machine was down because it was 6:03-04 AM and not even five minutes had passed since our shift started and since we all arrived, and I thought we were all settling into our workstations and about to turn the machine on, as is normal.

That bossy woman in blue yesterday, Friday, August 28th, at Automatic Machine 11, spoke to me with an air of superiority, arrogance, haughtiness, pride, and overbearing attitude. Just because she's my supervisor at ONE workstation doesn't give her the right to speak to me or treat me like that, nor to act with such an air of superiority.
Please teach your supervisors, or whoever they are, some manners, courtesy, and humility. Thank you.

one_star_reviews.text:
After my experience, I decided to move my relative to another care home, and honestly, I think it was one of the best decisions I could have made.

This care home is a very old, unwelcoming place with an atmosphere that I personally found very unpleasant. During my visits, I frequently heard a lot of noise and loud voices, to the point that I felt there was no real peace and quiet at any time of day.

As a family member, this situation worried me a lot because I believe a care home should offer elderly people an environment of calm, respect, tranquility, and well-being.

That's why I decided to look for another option and move my relative. The difference with the new care home has been enormous: much nicer and better-maintained facilities and, above all, a completely different atmosphere. There's a tranquility that you notice from the moment you walk in, and the staff and the ambiance inspire much more confidence.

After comparing both experiences, I personally wouldn't take my relative back to this place. Before choosing a care home for a loved one, I recommend that any family visit it in person, observe the atmosphere, and ask all the necessary questions before making a decision.

For me, after what I've been through, the change has been completely worth it.

The physical condition of this residence is deeply concerning and evokes profound sadness from the moment you step inside.

It's a rather old facility that hasn't received the necessary renovations or maintenance to provide a dignified home for the elderly. The lack of organization and cleanliness is evident in the administrative areas.
The director's office resembles an old warehouse, completely overflowing with papers, folders, and boxes piled up everywhere. Even more alarming is that this same disarray extends to the infirmary, a medical space that should be immaculate but is instead filled with junk, boxes, and accumulated documents, projecting a highly unprofessional and inappropriate image for a healthcare setting.

Finally, the furniture in the common areas, both indoors and outdoors, is completely worn out; the chairs where the residents sit are corroded, with very old and deteriorated wood. The elderly deserve to live in a clean, up-to-date, cheerful, and safe environment, not in a place that feels abandoned by management.

I lived here and I want to tell you what happens when my family calls. They're answered very rudely and in a rush, as if they don't want to talk to them. I feel very lonely in here. They ignore me, they don't pay attention to me, and many times I see them avoiding me. It seems to bother them when I ask for help. Besides, it's very noisy, and the caregivers spend all day shouting, which makes you very nervous. The worst part is that my phones and chargers keep disappearing. It's always the same: they take me to the shower, or I leave my phone charging in my room, and when I come back, it's gone. They always blame me and say I threw it out, but that's not true. They don't take care of our things, and you can't live like this. I'm in another residence now, and I'm very, very, very happy.

one_star_reviews.text:
⭐ IF I COULD GIVE ZERO STARS, I WOULD

A simply regrettable and shameful experience.

A year ago, in August, I entrusted this company with sending a package to Venezuela. It was supposed to arrive before December. Today, almost a year later, the shipment still hasn't arrived.

And this is where things get truly outrageous.

During all this time, instead of receiving a solution, I've received excuses, justifications, and further explanations. There always seems to be some circumstance that allows them to keep delaying the shipment. But curiously, for other shipments, there seems to be time, resources, and priority.

After a year, we're no longer talking about a simple delay. We're talking about a company that has demonstrated a worrying inability to resolve a problem they themselves created by accepting my shipment.

The most disappointing thing is the feeling that, once they have your money and your package, the customer ceases to matter.

Are there logistical problems? That's understandable.

Are there exceptional circumstances? Yes, there are.

What's impossible to understand is how those circumstances can become a permanent excuse for an entire year.

Because if a company needs a year to deliver a package and still can't provide a clear solution, then it should seriously reconsider what it means by "shipping service."

I'm not asking for a favor.

I'm demanding that they fulfill the service I paid for.

A customer shouldn't have to insist for months, constantly complain, and listen to explanations over and over again to get something as basic as knowing where their shipment is and when it will be delivered.

Patience has its limits. And a year far exceeds them.

My biggest mistake was trusting this company.

My advice to others is simple: before entrusting them with anything of value, think twice.

Because charging for receiving a shipment is easy.

The difficult part, it seems, is taking responsibility for delivering it.

For me, trust in this company is completely lost.

one_star_reviews.text:
I dropped off two packages. The first one went through without a problem, but the second one had a message saying the door hadn't closed properly. The screen said I could tap "open," and it opened, prompting me to deposit the package (it didn't specify that I should close that door and another one would open). I assumed it meant the same door again and closed it, but the screen then said a new door would open. So the package was left inside, unregistered, and I couldn't get it out. I called the customer service number countless times. At first, it was busy, and then after a few calls, it said they couldn't take my call. I was almost ready to give up, since I know they're not responsible if it's not registered, and they'd probably say I didn't deposit it because I have no proof. This happened to me with another locker (since it's not registered, I can't prove it's inside, and they do nothing). A guy came to drop off a package, and just then the hatch where my package had been left opened, and I was able to retrieve it. It was incredibly lucky; otherwise, I'm sure I would have lost it.
If you manage to drop off your package like the first one I put in without any problems, my rating would be higher, but my rating is based on the situation and because I realized that the customer service phone number they provide is completely useless.

one_star_reviews.text:
I do not recommend Alberto from "ALROMO Company". VERY BAD!

At first, they treat you well and quickly, but once you request quotes and ask for them to include materials and VAT,

Once they give you the quote, you have to wait a few weeks for them to come to your house to take measurements. Then, before starting the work, you tell them you need an invoice, and they tell you that VAT isn't included, even though you told them you needed it.

After that, they recalculate the prices, and the quote ends up being more expensive.

It wasn't just that, though. They raised the price for every little thing because they didn't seem to understand everything, saying things like:

"Oh! If it's not white, I have to charge you more."

"Oh! Sorry, I didn't see the VAT; VAT is separate."

"Oh! The dustpan isn't included in the quote; it's separate too."

Disappointing experience with their cancellation process. We had paid a deposit of €395, and although the house was eventually rebooked for the exact same dates and at a higher price, Naturaki only refunded 50% of the amount.

I fully understand that cancellation policies exist, but I believe that, in a situation where the accommodation ultimately didn't lose the reservation for those dates and was even resold at a higher price, it would have been reasonable to show more flexibility and refund 100% of the deposit.

I don't question their policy, but I do believe that customer service also involves the ability to assess each case individually and show some consideration when circumstances allow.

It's a shame, because the handling of this case has left us with a very negative impression.

This is the second time I've gone to the store intending to buy something. The first time I had a bad experience. Since you can't try on or exchange underwear (although the fitting rooms are sometimes left unattended, people still go in to try things on; you can check the security camera footage from around 6 PM today, where someone went in wearing underwear—the cashier noticed it as they were leaving), I asked for help finding my size. The cashier (with short hair and glasses) wasn't helpful and rushed me to choose because she had to keep ringing up and clearly had no intention of me buying anything. I went again this week, chose the items, and when I went to the register to pay, the same rude girl served me. She forced me to download the app to apply the discount for my accumulated points, and since there's no Wi-Fi or cell service inside, she told me to sort it out outside. When another line formed, I asked if I would have to wait in line again once I had the app, and she said yes (even though I had already waited in line). She has absolutely no desire to sell, she rushes you if you don't buy anything, and even if you leave the clothes behind, she doesn't care. The owners lose sales and customers with people like that, of course, she doesn't care...

I ended up going to the store on Príncipe Street where they helped me and treated me very well. I recommend going there directly; the girls there are much more enthusiastic and willing to help. :)

one_star_reviews.text:
Be aware of a possible scam!

We viewed a long-term rental in Guadalmina Baja, Calle 17 — 3 bedrooms, unfurnished, good price. It was advertised on Idealista, and we said we wanted to take it. We were then asked to pay a fee, first called a "reservation" or "management fee": €1,900 in cash (with parking), or €2,299 including VAT by bank transfer.

We said we didn't want to reserve it — we were happy to rent it — to which they replied that it doesn't work like that in Spain, and that you need to reserve it first, otherwise you may lose the deal, blah, blah.

We then asked for at least an invoice prior to payment, to see what servicing fees were included, and a copy of the rental contract before paying. The agency refused to provide either, and deleted messages from our WhatsApp chat. They then said they were not going to rent it to us, and that we had insulted and threatened them.

The apartment is still on the market now. Luckily, we didn't fall into that honey trap, but I'm not sure about others. Watch out!

one_star_reviews.text:
I bought a washer-dryer three months ago. Luckily, a friend was able to deliver it for me that day, saving me the shipping cost.

I used it three times before it stopped working. They told me it was fine, to bring it in and they'd fix it. I couldn't bring it in because I don't have a car. Then, in August, when I finally managed to get them to deliver it one day, they had just switched to their August hours and weren't open in the afternoon. I complained, explaining that I couldn't bring it in myself, that it didn't work for me, and they didn't offer me any other option, like picking it up (which they're legally obligated to do). They just insisted I bring it in myself... and they only gave me a three-month warranty. The law states that the seller is responsible for all shipping, repair, and other repair costs while the product is under warranty. And it establishes a minimum one-year warranty.

**Response: "As we informed you when you purchased it, warranties are honored in-store when the customer picks it up themselves, since we don't know where they might take it. If they take it to Madrid, what do you expect us to do, travel to Madrid as you yourself stated? We also remind you that warranties cover breakdowns (not misuse) or damage or DROPS of the washing machine during transport... as is the case here."

DROPS? It's incredibly unprofessional to, on top of deceiving people in your business, then come online to excuse your poor work, implying that it fell during transport.
How do you know it fell? Have you seen it to tell me if it has any dents or scratches?

Or is this what you do with all your customers to save money? Claim it's due to misuse and wash your hands of it?

You blocked me on WhatsApp and my personal Instagram. I messaged you on my other Instagram account, and you haven't even responded. I think this already says a lot about you and your professionalism.

And if we're going by the law, regarding your question about whether you have to go to Madrid, well, it's understood that if you have to go pick it up, you'll go... I also have to say, you're giving a rather surreal example... Who's going to buy a washing machine in their town to take it all the way to Madrid? It makes no sense, but oh well...

Oh, and when I bought it, I wasn't informed or told anything about it, and I didn't ask many questions because I was in a hurry. They only told me the price, the payment methods, and that if they delivered it to my house it would be an extra €40.

Anyway... even to open a business, YOU HAVE TO KNOW WHAT YOU'RE DOING!!!!

one_star_reviews.text: I had never had any problems with them and was very happy with the bank until I was scammed out of €4,700 from my account by phone, a scam I was responsible for falling for. The problem arose when I went to the branch and felt attacked and judged by the young woman who served me. She told me that this was why they insisted we do everything through online banking, because it meant I had given them my online banking credentials (a lie). I'm someone who NEVER pays online directly with my card; I always use intermediaries and other methods to prevent my Visa from being cloned. I'm responsible for the transactions they made because they caught me off guard after more than a month of sleep deprivation. But I haven't given my access codes to anyone, much less all the personal information these people told me about over the phone. Their response was, "That's because you clicked on a phishing search engine." Of course, I should know that, because when I search "Pibank" on Google, the bank appears first. Maybe on the day I'm accessing it, they cloned the website, creating a mirror image, and are stealing my data. They repeatedly told me it was all done through my phone, not the search engine (as if I were stupid), until I finally got fed up and told them that the online access to my bank account is because the ownership certificates and tax returns for the tax authorities CANNOT be obtained from the website. The app certificates they recently requested for multiple documents related to my maternity leave and tax agency benefits are unacceptable. So, between that and the fact that they've washed their hands of the matter, I'm extremely dissatisfied with the bank for their treatment of me and the complete lack of security they offer.

Another bank to add to the zero-recommendation list.
Between cybercriminals and them washing their hands of the matter, they've stolen €4,000 from me. Disgusting.
